title: Composed diagonal-bit bootstrap: the pricing model that called PR205's banked row, audits the queue, and prices the next ladder of κ gains
body:
Under the retained interfaces of the pinned suppliers, this composes **#200**'s
certified bit supplier with **#193/#194**'s complex word through **#194**'s
unchanged assembly and prices it with **#185**'s finite ordinary leaf:

$$\kappa=\frac{1693287}{2500000000}=6.773148\cdot10^{-4},$$

**+0.1826%** over #197's standing claim and **+0.0639%** over the composition as
#202 published it. Adds `research/composed-diagonal-bit-bootstrap/` and one
workflow. The package now does three things: prices this composition, **audits the
banked rows that overtook it**, and **prices the ladder of moves that can still
raise kappa**.

## The banked rows arrived, and this package's model called one exactly

This composition was priced at 15:33 UTC. Its lever model then predicted what
banking this word's 2,200 rank-60 exterior corrections would be worth — a row with
`W_per_vertex = 56402/3`, deficit unchanged at 1,936, no rank-60 child left and
coarse saving `683528191056257/10^18`. Within the half hour that row was built and
opened as #205, which states that exact saving and credits this PR as its target;
#206 prices the same row with PR186's entrance banks, and #207 adds 302
coordinated frame changes on top:

| PR | author | kappa | row |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **#207** | Dugongue | **6.831904550365e-4** | the banked word after 302 coordinated frame changes; current frontier |
| #205 | rohanarun | 6.83061299399923e-4 | PR200's word with its rank-60 exterior corrections banked — the value modelled here |
| #206 | EcmaXp | 6.830611e-4 | the same row via PR186's entrance banks |
| #202 | chafreaky | 6.768823e-4 | the same composition as this PR with the legacy atom wrapper |
| #197 | evmckinney9 | 6.76080316519385e-4 | packed #187's residuals + #193 complex + the finite leaf |
| this | Maxime Fleury | 6.773148e-4 | #200's bit + #193's complex + #185's finite leaf on #194's assembly |

`audit.py` prices #205's, #206's and #207's rows from byte-identical copies of
their certificates under `references/queue/` and requires each result to appear
**verbatim** in the certificate it came from. All three reproduce to the last
digit, and each sits at its own word's ceiling: with the bit branch binding,
`kappa = C/(1+C)` and there is no pricing room left in any of them.

## New ways to raise kappa, priced

PR184's assembly takes `a = min(bit leaf, (1-1e-9)*C_complex - 1e-10)` and returns
`kappa = a/(1+a)` on the `10^-10` grid, so **the smaller branch is the whole
constraint** and a gain on the stronger side is worth nothing until the other side
catches up. Today the bit branch binds at `6.831904e-4` while the complex side caps
at `7.004273e-4`: **+2.52% is available with no complex-side work at all.**

`targets.py` prices the moves that get there. For a fixed stock and deficit the
coarse saving is `C = (1 - mass/(W m)) / L` with `L` the rank-mass-weighted mean of
`ln(m/r)`, so the lever is `L`: a ledger whose residual dirt sits in fewer, larger
children. Soaking every child of rank at or below a threshold into the largest
admissible child gives, on the queue's own rows:

| soak | bit coarse saving | complex coarse saving | kappa | gain | binds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| today | 136731504666219/2e17 | 350459221139329/5e17 | 6.831904e-4 | — | bit |
| bit only, rank-1 | 792978386838687/10^18 | — | 7.004273e-4 | +2.52% | complex |
| both, rank-1 | 792978386838687/10^18 | 814442339516203/10^18 | 7.923515e-4 | +15.98% | bit |
| both, rank-2 | 898167154125293/10^18 | 918515942111545/10^18 | 8.973611e-4 | +31.35% | bit |
| both, rank-3 | 981391149202381/10^18 | 1041436537175764/10^18 | 9.804289e-4 | +43.51% | bit |
| both, rank-4 | 1015042828910707/10^18 | 1112905588874264/10^18 | 1.014014e-3 | +48.42% | bit |
| both, rank-8 | 1096975618911405/10^18 | 1243672552482743/10^18 | 1.095774e-3 | +60.39% | bit |
| both, rank-16 | 1178908992537918/10^18 | 1367642974340202/10^18 | 1.177521e-3 | +72.36% | bit |
| cheapest ledgers | 1207154248293627/10^18 | 1391081382485139/10^18 | 1.205699e-3 | +76.48% | — |

The cheapest step is smaller than the table suggests. The bit word needs a coarse
saving of `7.009184e-4` to stop binding, and `targets.py` bisects the smallest-child
population to find the least that delivers it: **moving 57/1000 of the mass in the
bit word's rank-1 children into rank-22 children takes its coarse saving to
`7.009717e-4`**, past the complex word, for `kappa = 7.004273e-4` (+2.52%). The whole
population (377,316 rank-1 children, 9.3% of the rank mass) is worth +16% on its own,
and the complex word's own 87,534 rank-1 children (11% of its mass) do the same for
its side, `7.009184e-4` to `8.144423e-4` (+16.2%).

**What has to change is the child inventory, not the packing.** #207's bank proof
settles the packing side itself: its banks tile width 72 exactly with the word's two
residual families (`6 x rank-4 + 2 x rank-24`, or `3 x rank-24`), and it states that
the current word "has exactly the 4/24 residual families and both tile 72 exactly ...
there is no new LP improvement to add". The children the moment actually charges are
the word's own retained children — internal, source, target, center, compensating and
terminal-substitution children — and it is their inventory, set by the weighted
compilation and by the frame schedule, that holds `L` above `ln(m/22)`.


**All of it is MODELLED, NOT CONSTRUCTED**: no ledger is built here, and each rung
is a shape the assembly would price this way, computed from the queue's certified
rows. The calculator is checked two ways — it equals PR184's own `assemble()` on the
vendored pair, and it reproduces #205's and #207's published kappa to within one
grid step — so a rung is a usable target, in the same way the banked row was.

## What the composition itself does

Exactly one operation: **pricing**. #200 certified a strictly stronger bit word —
coarse saving `677773948354561/10^18 = 6.77773948355e-4` against #189's
`6.68298937775631e-4` — but published it only with its own complex word, where the
complex branch binds. Composed with the source-assisted complex word
(`219037/312500000 = 7.009184e-4`) the bit branch binds, and PR185's wrapper then
removes the `4.33e-7` of slack PR184's legacy leaf leaves below the coarse saving:

| depth | bit leaf | kappa | vs #197 | vs the unbootstrapped composition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 (legacy wrapper, = #200's and #202's value) | 6.77340866500955e-4 | 6768823/10000000000 = 6.768823e-4 | +0.1186% | — |
| 1 | 6.77773606501196e-4 | 1354629/2000000000 = 6.773145e-4 | +0.1825% | +0.0639% |
| 2, 3, 8 | 6.77773899999987e-4 | **1693287/2500000000 = 6.773148e-4** | **+0.1826%** | +0.0639% |

The priced bit profile has `m = 72`, `W = 20634`, rank deficit 1936 and 34 terminal
sinks; the claim sits **3.37e-11** below the word's own ceiling
`C/(1+C) = 6.7731483368e-4`, under one `10^-10` selection step, with depths 2, 3 and
8 returning the same grid value. The bit profile, the complex word, the 47-constraint
assembly and the leaf recurrence are the suppliers' and #185's; nothing is re-derived.

`levers.py` is the model behind all of this: it solves the paid-moment inequality
exactly over the rationals and checks itself against three published values, all
reproduced **exactly** because it prices with PR200's own enclosure module
(`references/pr200/interval_moment.py`, vendored byte-identically):

| row | W | D | model = published | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PR187's word, unpacked | 63,324 | 5,808 | 167724995262213/250000000000000000 = 6.70899981048852e-4 | PR187's certificate |
| PR187's word, banked | 57,824 | 5,808 | 676537710350481/10^18 = 6.76537710350481e-4 | #197's **certified** packed word |
| PR200's word, unpacked | 61,902 | 5,808 | 677773948354561/10^18 = 6.77773948354561e-4 | #200's certificate |

## Verification

```bash
python3 -B research/composed-diagonal-bit-bootstrap/verify.py
```

Runs from the package directory alone with only the standard library, on Python
3.11 and 3.13, and pins every byte against `SOURCE.json`. It checks that the
certificate regenerates exactly; that depth 0 equals #200's and #202's value; that
PR184's grid legacy leaf against #200's published atom wrapper differs by exactly
one grid step at depth 0 and nothing once bootstrapped; that the claim beats #197
and sits inside one grid step of `C/(1+C)`; that the leaf tolls hold in closed form
and the assembly's own minimum margin excludes the next grid point; that three
corruption controls are refused; that the lever model reproduces its three
published references exactly; **that the audit reproduces #205's, #206's and #207's
own certified coarse savings verbatim**; and **that the target ladder reproduces two
published kappa values, stays monotone and never presents itself as a
construction**. A clean Linux clone of the branch passes and leaves the tree
unchanged; the whole harness runs in about seven seconds.

## Scope and limits

* The physical complex and bit words, their frames, sinks and paid moments are the
  suppliers' certified artifacts, vendored byte-identically and **priced, not
  rebuilt or replayed**. This PR does not re-run their checks, including #205's,
  #206's and #207's: it prices the rows they certify.
* The wrapper is PR185's construction, not one built here; the banked rows are
  #205's, #206's and #207's, not built here; every rung of the ladder is a target,
  not a construction.
* Conditional on PR184's finite bridge and closed-form acceptance arithmetic and on
  the retained contracts of the pinned suppliers. The full multiplication theorem
  remains conditional.
* Dependent on unmerged lines (#200's bit supplier, the #193/#194 complex/assembly
  line, and the #205/#206/#207 bank line).
* Not claimed: a new word, a new all-size hypothesis, priority, or the frontier.
  The frontier belongs to the banked rows above.
